evidence.title: 2000 Welsh Cup Final
evidence.text: The 2000 Welsh Cup Final saw Bangor City win the Welsh Cup after beating Cwmbran Town 1–0 at Racecourse Ground in the 113th Welsh Cup Final.

evidence.title: Welsh League Cup
evidence.text: The Welsh League Cup (also known as the League of Wales Cup, Welsh Premier League Cup or The Word Cup) is a cup competition in Welsh football organised by the Welsh Premier League.

evidence.title: Welsh League Cup
evidence.text: The competition was established in 1992 and is considered to be the second-most important domestic cup competition for Welsh football clubs, after the older and more prestigious Welsh Cup.

evidence.title: Welsh League Cup
evidence.text: Unlike the Welsh Cup, where 135 teams entered in 2008–09, the competition is only open to the members of the Welsh Premier League and a very select few other clubs.

evidence.title: Welsh League Cup
evidence.text: It should not be confused with the Welsh Football League Cup, which is for the clubs in the Welsh Football League, which despite its name only covers the south and centre of Wales.

evidence.title: 1980 Welsh Cup Final
evidence.text: The 1980 Welsh Cup Final was the final of the 93rd season of the main domestic football cup competition in Wales, the Welsh Cup.

evidence.title: 1980 Welsh Cup Final
evidence.text: The final was contested between Newport County and Shrewsbury Town over two legs.

evidence.title: 1980 Welsh Cup Final

evidence.text: The team play in League Two, the fourth tier of the English football league system.

evidence.title: Newport County A.F.C.
evidence.text: Most recently reformed in 1989, the club is a continuation of the Newport County club which was founded in 1912 and was a founder member of the Football League's new Third Division in 1920.

evidence.title: Richard Johnson (rugby)
evidence.text: Richard Johnston, born (26-02-1980) in Neath, Wales, first started his career at Neath RFC in 1998 where he gained representative honours for Wales under 18/19's.

evidence.title: Richard Johnson (rugby)
evidence.text: In 2000 Richard signed for Pontypridd RFC where he spent three years.

evidence.title: Richard Johnson (rugby)
evidence.text: In his time at Ponty, Richard was selected for Wales U21's and Wales 7's and was involved in the squad that won the Welsh Cup in 2002 and narrowly lost to Sale in the Parker Pen European Shield Final.

evidence.title: Richard Johnson (rugby)
evidence.text: After regional rugby was formed he returned to Neath RFC winning the league twice and Welsh Cup in a three-year stint.

evidence.title: Richard Johnson (rugby)
evidence.text: Richard then changed codes, signing for Crusader RL and won 4 caps for Wales.

evidence.title: Richard Johnson (rugby)
evidence.text: He also played on the 7's circuit playing for Samurai 7's, White Hart Marauders, Crusaders and Scorpions.

evidence.title: Richard Johnson (rugby)
evidence.text: In 2007 Richard left rugby to pursue a career outside sport but continues to play on the 7's circuit and now vets competitions.

evidence.title: 2010 Welsh Cup Final
evidence.text: The 2010 Welsh Cup Final was the final of the 124th season of the main domestic football cup competition in Wales, the Welsh Cup.

evidence.title: 2010 Welsh Cup Final
evidence.text: The final was played at Parc y Scarlets in Llanelli on 1 May 2010 and marked the second time the final has been staged at the stadium.

evidence.title: 2010 Welsh Cup Final
evidence.text: The match was contested by Port Talbot Town, who beat Bala Town 1–0 in their semi-final, and Bangor City who beat Prestatyn Town 2–0 in their semi-final.

evidence.title: 2011 Welsh Cup Final

evidence.title: 2011 Welsh Cup Final
evidence.text: The match was contested by Bangor City, who beat Gap Connah's Quay 1-0 in their semi-final, and Llanelli who beat The New Saints 1-0 in their semi-final.
